newsitem.title: USA: Calif Gov. vetoes bankruptcy oversight legislation.
newsitem.headline: Calif Gov. vetoes bankruptcy oversight legislation.

text.p: California Governor Pete Wilson vetoed legislation late on Monday that would have increased state oversight over local governments seeking bankruptcy protection.
Wilson, a Republican, vetoed Senate Bill 349, which would have established the Local Agency Bankruptcy Committee, a spokesman for the governor said.
Under the measure, local agencies in the state that intended to file for bankruptcy would have had to seek the committee's approval before petitioning the courts.
The measure was introduced in the wake of Orange County, Calif.,'s unprecedented bankruptcy filing.

Orange County filed for protection under Chapter 9 of the federal Bankruptcy Code on December 6, 1994, after investment losses of more than $1.6 billion. The county emerged from bankruptcy in June of this year.

State Treasurer Matt Fong had strongly urged Wilson to sign the legislation. "Before a local agency takes such a serious step as bankruptcy, that so dramatically affects the state, state level oversight should occur," Fong said.
The state's Department of Finance was opposed to the legislation. The department argued that the measure would have usurped power from local elected officials.
